lesson_title: The Party, the Photograph and the Leaking Bucket
hook_text: Every house party ends with thirty people in the kitchen. That's your population exam, sorted.
clip_script: Why does every party end with thirty people crammed in the kitchen and nobody on the stoep? Because people drift to where the food is. Now zoom out: that IS South Africa's population map. Gauteng is the kitchen — the smallest province holding a quarter of the country, because a gold rush that started in 1886 never stopped serving jobs. The Northern Cape is the stoep — huge, beautiful, two people per square kilometre, because no rain means no farms means no work. Next, the country's family photo: a population pyramid is everyone lined up by age, babies at the bottom. Wide bottom row, empty top — young and growing fast. Straight column — rich, old, and short of workers. South Africa sits in between, base narrowing, with a visible notch the HIV years cut into the young adults before the world's biggest treatment programme turned it around. And through it all runs the water: a country on half the world's average rainfall, carrying its supply in a leaking bucket — a third of city water lost through broken pipes — moving mountain water from Lesotho to Gauteng's taps, and counting down to Day Zero in Cape Town before the savings kicked in. The twist that ties it together: the people who came to the kitchen for work got the leftover land — and the leftover land is the floodplain. Population, settlement, water: one story. Learn it as one story and the exam reads itself.
visual_style: A buzzing house party seen from above morphing into a glowing map of South Africa with Gauteng as the crowded kitchen; a stadium crowd arranging itself into pyramid shapes; water animating through pipes with glowing leak points; a countdown clock over Cape Town easing back from zero.
mood: Sharp, sociable, building to a serious final beat.
pacing: Party joke opens fast, map reveal lands it, pyramid beat plays visual, water beat tightens, the one-story twist closes with weight.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and carry the whole human geography year in three pictures.
